incident-bot: PAGING: EU-WEST2 p99 tail spike and streaming stalls detected for router->lb path. start: 2026-03-15T09:24:05Z. Auto-alert threshold breached (p99 > 1.2s) :rotating_light:

maria_oncall: I'm on it. joining call in 2. Can someone grab initial graphs?

leo_sre: grabbing traces now. looks like misrouted requests to a small set of nodes in eu-west2 causing queuing. heatmap shows ~4x traffic to node-set-7.

sam_runtime: seeing increased queue depth on router shard 7, eviction/backpressure kicking in intermittently. Noting a routing policy fallback triggered ~09:23:58Z.

anya_product: any customer impact? sales reported a chat customer complaining about slow streaming.

kevin_support: confirmed one customer reported sessions stalling for ~15-30s. CS ticket #CS-9932 opened. Not wide yet but affecting a few high-traffic accounts.

maria_oncall: decision: open a live-bridge if we can't mitigate in 10 min. leo, can you verify whether it's policy-induced or a health flake?

leo_sre: quick diff of routing table changes: a recent rollout to routing-policy v5 pushed a prefactor weight change that accidentally assigns higher affinity to region-local routing for a subset of keys. The affected keys are high-QPS prefixes -> hot-route.

sam_runtime: that matches logs. we have repeated "policy-assign: local_affinity boost" events for prefixes with streaming sessions. also KV cache thrashing on a few workers.

maria_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) rollback routing-policy v5 to v4 for eu-west2 only (non-global) 2) temporarily throttle affinity weight for local routing 3) shift traffic away from node-set-7 if rollback not fast enough.

raj_devex: rollback command below (use canary-first):
```
# rollback routing-policy v5 -> v4 in eu-west2
redwoodctl routing-policy set --region eu-west2 --policy v4 --dry-run=false --reason "paging mitigation"
```

leo_sre: executing rollback now. patch to control plane applied at 09:26:10Z. pushing change to route distributor.

ops-bot: CONTROL PLANE: routing-policy change applied to eu-west2 (v5 -> v4) by leo_sre at 2026-03-15T09:26:11Z.

sam_runtime: monitoring... initial metrics: p99 dropping from 1.35s -> 0.75s over 1 minute but p95 still elevated. streaming stalls decreased but not fully resolved.

maria_oncall: good. continue to watch. if p99 < 0.9s and no new stalls for 5m we'll close paging.

kevin_support: updated CS ticket: "mitigation in progress; temporary routing rollback applied. We're monitoring for recovery." Customer notified.

anya_product: flagging product incident page and prepping status blurb if sustained impact.

leo_sre: small tail remains. digging deeper: LB envoy metrics show a small subset of connections (client-ids) with persistent long-lived streams pinned to worker 7; worker 7's thread pool nearing saturation for long-poll handlers.

sam_runtime: looks like prefix hash mapping + local-affinity created stickiness -> hotstream fanout. We should consider rebalancing shards or ejecting worker 7 temporarily from rotation.

maria_oncall: can we eject worker 7 temporarily? cost is some warm-up but avoids prolonged stalls.

sam_runtime: ejecting worker 7 from active pool at 09:29:05Z. will route new requests away while existing streams drain.

ops-bot: WORKER ACTION: worker-7 marked DRAINING by sam_runtime at 2026-03-15T09:29:06Z.

leo_sre: immediate effect: queue depth on remaining workers rebalanced. p99 now 0.42s, streaming stalls dropped to baseline.

maria_oncall: excellent. continue to monitor for 10m. prepare postmortem notes.

kevin_support: customer says performance improving now. will follow up after 10m to confirm.

anya_product: we should rollback the global rollout flag for routing-policy v5 until we patch the affinity calculation. add to backlog: verify hash distribution invariants and add load-tests for prefix skew.

raj_devex: creating a quick test harness to reproduce skew with prefix-heavy traffic.

leo_sre: initial root cause: routing-policy v5 introduced a per-prefix affinity boost that didn't account for high-cardinality prefixes (small cardinality but high QPS). result: traffic collapsed onto subset of local nodes -> hot route -> queueing -> tail latency and streaming stalls.

maria_oncall: action items (short):
- leo: write mitigation timeline and logs + mark worker-7 drain events (done).
- sam: verify worker-7 health and reintroduce as warmed when safe.
- raj: run stress harness to reproduce and attach to ticket.
- anya: coordinate release note + restrict v5 rollout.
- kevin: confirm customers recovered and close CS-9932 when verified.

sam_runtime: reintroducing worker-7 in warm pool at 09:40:12Z after health checks.

ops-bot: WORKER ACTION: worker-7 marked ACTIVE by sam_runtime at 2026-03-15T09:40:13Z.

maria_oncall: closing paging: p99 stable at 0.45s for last 6 minutes, streaming success rate normal. Closing at 09:46:29Z.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: eu-west2 routing tail spike. root cause: routing-policy v5 affinity boost -> hot-route -> worker queueing. // Summary: rollback regional policy + ejected hot worker to drain; customer impact limited to a small set of accounts; CS ticket updated.

anya_product: follow-up: schedule a postmortem doc and link to PR that fixes affinity logic. Also add automated alert for prefix-hotness (flux across nodes) to detect this earlier.

leo_sre: attaching logs and sample traces to postmortem.

kevin_support: CS-9932: customer confirmed recovery, closing ticket at 09:52Z.

maria_oncall: thanks all. nice rapid coordination. leaving notes for retrospective.

raj_devex: test harness PR opened: #PR-1012. includes synthetic prefix-heavy workload generator.

sam_runtime: follow-up ops: add safe-guard cap on per-prefix affinity weight in control plane.

incident-bot: ACTIONS_LOGGED: [rollback-policy-eu-west2, drain-worker-7, reintroduce-worker-7, create-harness-pr-1012, restrict-v5-rollout]
